reviews.body:
From my perspective this can be merged. `TextQuery("the a an")` now raises the same `ValueError` as `AggregateHybridQuery`, and the shared helper is byte for byte the old tokenizer plus that check, so no other query changes.

non-blocking: the MCP fulltext tool builds a `TextQuery` too, and `map_exception` turns the new `ValueError` into a clean invalid-request error, which beats the Redis syntax error it got before.

```
$ python rv_repro.py        # construction half of the #821 repro, base 930c14e vs head c18f796
base: 'the a an' -> @body:()
head: 'the a an' -> ValueError: text string cannot be empty after removing stopwords

$ pytest -q --noconftest tests/unit/test_text_query_weights.py tests/unit/test_query_types.py tests/unit/test_aggregation_types.py   # head, Python 3.12
83 passed, 1 skipped in 1.21s

$ (same, base query.py, head tests)
FAILED tests/unit/test_text_query_weights.py::test_text_query_rejects_empty_tokenized_text[the a an-english]
4 failed, 79 passed, 1 skipped in 0.62s
# not run: live Redis, the integration suite
```

I'll send the escaped-token fix as the follow-up once this is in.

review_comments.body:
This builds a new `FullTextQueryHelper` on every tokenize, and each one re-validates stopwords and weights that `TextQuery` has already parsed. In my measurements that takes `str(TextQuery(...))` from 5.8 µs to 18.4 µs for a 9-word query, and from 46 µs to 99 µs for 200 words.

It also leaves two copies of the same logic: `_set_stopwords` and `_parse_text_weights` here duplicate the helper's `_get_stopwords` and `_parse_text_weights`. And because validation now runs on every build, mutating the returned containers turns into a build-time error: `q.stopwords.add(1); str(q)` now raises `TypeError`, where before it was ignored.

Could `TextQuery` hold a single `self._ft_helper` built in `__init__`, the way `HybridQuery` (`hybrid.py:143`) and `AggregateHybridQuery` (`aggregate.py:175`) do? `stopwords`, `text_weights` and `set_text_weights` would forward to it (keeping the `_built_query_string = None` reset), `_tokenize_and_escape_query` becomes a thin forwarder, and the duplicate methods and the `get_stopwords` import can go.

Running this before `set_filter` means an argument type error now loses to the content check: `TextQuery("the", "b", filter_expression=123)` raised the filter `TypeError` before and now raises the stopwords `ValueError`. Could this move after `self.set_filter(...)`?

The result is also thrown away and recomputed in `_build_query_string`, so every query tokenizes twice. With a held helper (see the comment on line 1426), it's worth keeping the result rather than tokenizing again.

`TextQuery("", "b", stopwords=None)` raises "text string cannot be empty after removing stopwords", although no stopwords are configured. `AggregateHybridQuery` checks `if not text.strip()` separately (`aggregate.py:164`) and gives a plain "text string cannot be empty". Could `TextQuery` do the same, so the stopwords message only appears when stopwords actually removed everything?

This file covers field and text weights; the empty-after-stopwords test fits better in `test_query_types.py`, next to the existing `TextQuery` stopword assertions (around line 256). The new coverage in `test_text_query_preserves_escaping_and_updated_weights` is that `set_text_weights` resets the cached query string, so the test name should say that.

Fixed in 8237317. TextQuery now owns one FullTextQueryHelper; stopwords, text_weights and set_text_weights delegate to it, with cache invalidation retained. Removed duplicate stopword and weight parsing and the unused import. A regression confirms rebuilds do not revalidate mutated weights.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Fixed in 8237317. Content validation runs after set_filter, preserving the filter TypeError. Construction retains the built query string; a counted-tokenizer regression confirms construction plus first rendering tokenizes once, and set_text_weights invalidates it.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Fixed in 8237317. Empty or whitespace-only text now raises the plain empty-text ValueError, including when stopwords=None. Added explicit regression coverage.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Fixed in 8237317. Moved stopword construction tests next to the TextQuery stopword assertions in test_query_types.py; renamed the weight test to test_set_text_weights_resets_cached_query_string.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

This test pins that writing into the dict returned by `query.text_weights` is silently accepted. That's a side effect of the property returning the helper's own dict, not behaviour we want to promise. Could it go?

This test counts calls to the private `_tokenize_and_escape_query` through monkeypatching, so it breaks whenever the tokenizer is restructured (#833 already changes it). The behaviour that matters, that `set_text_weights` resets the cached query string, is already covered by `test_set_text_weights_resets_cached_query_string` (`test_text_query_weights.py:125`). Could this one go too?

comments.body: I can get this PR merged as soon as those last comments are addressed 🙌

Fixed in b990e76:

- `tests/unit/test_query_types.py` (weights mutation): removed `test_text_query_does_not_revalidate_mutated_weights_on_rebuild`, so direct mutation of the returned dictionary is no longer pinned as supported behaviour.
- `tests/unit/test_query_types.py` (tokenization): removed `test_text_query_tokenizes_once_until_weights_change`; the existing `test_set_text_weights_resets_cached_query_string` still covers cache invalidation.

Selected query tests pass: 85 passed, 1 skipped.
